parsed.explanation: Decriminalisation since 2021 and punishable sexual-orientation discrimination remove the severest criminal exposure, and no trans-specific entry, facility or universal-exposure rule is documented. Against that, a June 2024 police attack on a trans woman with injury, arbitrary detention and degrading treatment, plus 2024 shadow-report findings of persistent discrimination and under-investigated violence, show state-perpetrated harm and weak recourse in practice. No border friction, prison-placement, facilities or minor-specific evidence is documented, so uncertainty remains, but the documented police/custody risk keeps this below the reduced-risk tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry/visa rule documented; resident marker-change route unresolved and not shown to affect foreign passports.
entry_documents.protection: No criminal exposure under sexual-offence provisions after decriminalisation.
entry_documents.interaction: Unresolved resident registration position does not document traveller document rejection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: June 2024: trans woman attacked by police, injured, arbitrarily detained and degradingly treated.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Case under investigation by judicial military police; outcome not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police custody is the documented pathway from outing to detention/harm; no prison-placement data.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No shelters, safe houses or gender-neutral facilities recorded; no facility-access rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational variation documented; absence is a sourcing gap, not evidence of uniformity or safety.

care_services.exposure: 2024 shadow report: persistent discrimination in health, education and employment; health-access issues raised to UN committee.
care_services.protection: Discrimination on sexual-orientation grounds punishable; people with HIV entitled to health care, but trans-specific service protection not enumerated.
care_services.interaction: Statutory protection exists on paper but implementation gap is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Constitution does not enumerate gender/sexual orientation; protection rests on general identity, privacy, liberty and expression rights.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 Penal Code decriminalised same-sex conduct and criminalises orientation discrimination up to two years.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Stronger statutory package than constitutional layer; law does not criminalise trans identity/expression.

minors_guardians.interaction: No youth/minor findings on travel, medication or education in dossier.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Under-investigated violence documented in 2024 shadow report; police were perpetrators in June 2024 case.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Investigation of that case underway; no prosecution outcome documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State as perpetrator plus under-investigation weakens recourse for street or custody violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Shadow report documents gap between statutory protections and practice; no itemised incidents, dates or penalties.
remedies_unknowns.protection: NGOs exist and one group officially recognised since 2018; general constitutional rights available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies on paper exist but documented effectiveness for trans visitors is unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in brief detention/discrimination with formal protections, but here police inflicted injury and degrading treatment and no apology/compensation or reliable release remedy is documented, so lower.
Higher than 0.55-A because no routine registration/checkpoint system, overnight holding regime or mateix of universal exposure is documented, and criminalisation has been removed.

Lower than 0.75-C: no documented accepted foreign documents, respectful border practice, written detention reasons, counsel access or compensation remedy; police abuse and under-investigation dominate.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: decriminalisation and anti-discrimination law lower the ceiling of harm, removing imprisonment/execution pathways tied to sexuality law. The operative risk is not universal state exposure but episodic police violence, arbitrary detention and degrading treatment, compounded by persistent service discrimination and under-investigated violence. With no documented traveller-facing protections actually working, no subnational, facilities, custody-placement or minor-specific evidence, and a recent state-perpetrated case, consequences after outing remain moderate-to-major despite formal protections.
